command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It performs only one 60-second CPU burst and one uninstrumented sleep, uses unsafe SSH, tails output, and its generic risk claims DIMM/disk stress absent from this source. It cannot prove repeated transition or idle recovery.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After the duration ruling, use a monotonic bounded loop around the exact approved 60-second CPU burst and 60-second observed idle interval, recording full output, worker exit, settling metrics and incremental events per cycle.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source's 225 workers and one-minute stress/idle intervals remain. Eight hours versus the `idle-24-hrs` Script identity and cycle-count versus wall-clock interpretation await Engineering Decision.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Give every transition a cycle ID, measure actual burst and idle boundaries, require worker exit plus defined load/frequency/temperature settling, and stop rather than allowing schedule drift or overlap.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes idle an observed recovery state, exposes duration conflict and records transition-specific health instead of one uptime sample.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A sleep can expire while stress workers remain or while the system is throttled, so one healthy final uptime cannot prove hundreds of successful load-to-idle transitions.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Rapid repeated load changes can expose VRM/power, frequency-governor, thermal and watchdog faults; a wall-clock run may complete fewer cycles than a fixed-count run because command overhead accumulates.

project_override_considerations: Approve eight or 24 hours, wall-clock deadline versus exact cycles (nominally 240 two-minute cycles for eight hours before overhead), literal 225 workers, idle-settling thresholds, interval tolerance and private Script revision/behavior.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and 480-minute Machine Time require eight hours, but the referenced private Script path identifies `idle-24-hrs`. This changes exposure and nominal cycle count and requires an authoritative ruling while Master remains unchanged.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The alternating CPU/idle purpose and one-minute phases are clear. Duration, load suitability and recovery thresholds are identifiable owner inputs, so classification remains REQUIRES.

review_improvement: Corrects DeepSeek's unrelated DIMM/disk framing, exposes the eight-versus-24-hour contradiction and turns every idle interval into measured recovery evidence rather than an unverified sleep.
independent_technical_reasoning: The stress-to-idle edge is the observation target. A process can overrun its nominal timeout, and scheduler load can delay the next sample; without explicit worker-exit and monotonic timestamps, cycles may overlap or drift. Settling of load, frequency, temperature and power must be evaluated before the next burst, or the test degenerates into near-continuous stress rather than transition cycling.
